Share on X Telegram Determined to test its election technology, personnel and operational readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said it would deploy 598 polling units across Delta state for a nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise. It noted that any technical shortcomings identified during the simulation would be documented and addressed before the actual elections. Delta State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Sir Etekamba Udo Umoren, made the disclosure on Friday during a press conference at the commission’s conference hall in Asaba, the state capital. The exercise, scheduled for Saturday, November 28, will cover all 25 local government areas of the state, with two polling units selected from each registration area (RA). Umoren said the exercise is a critical component of INEC’s preparations for the 2027 elections, providing an opportunity to assess the performance and reliability of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) under different environmental and operational conditions. According to him, polling units will open at 7:30am, while accreditation will commence at 8am and close at 2:30pm. He explained that the selection of polling units across the 25 LGAs was intended to ensure broad geographical coverage and enable the commission to assess election-day operations at the grassroots level. The REC said the exercise would test the functionality of BVAS and other relevant electoral technologies, including the accreditation process, voting procedures, result recording and transmission. Umoren said that beyond technology, the electoral umpire would use the exercise to evaluate the preparedness of its personnel, especially their knowledge of polling procedures and ability to handle election materials, conduct accreditation, manage voting processes and undertake result-related responsibilities. He stressed that electoral officials must demonstrate professionalism, discipline and neutrality while adhering strictly to established electoral guidelines. He stated that the exercise would also provide an opportunity to assess the commission’s logistics, including the timely deployment of personnel, election materials, equipment and other resources to designated polling units. Umoren said special attention would be paid to transportation, movement of materials, polling unit setup and the ability of officials to operate within stipulated timelines. He noted that identified logistical gaps would be addressed ahead of the 2027 general polls. On stakeholder participation, the REC called on political parties, security agencies, the media, civil society organisations, community leaders and other stakeholders to support the exercise and promote public understanding of its objectives. He urged the media to report the exercise accurately and responsibly to prevent misconceptions, particularly the erroneous impression that it is an actual election. Umoren also called on political actors, community leaders, youths and members of the public to maintain peace, cooperate with electoral officials and refrain from any conduct capable of disrupting the exercise. He said INEC would collaborate with relevant security agencies to ensure a peaceful and orderly exercise. The REC further disclosed that the commission would closely monitor the exercise, evaluate its performance and obtain feedback from electoral officials, observers, stakeholders and technical personnel. According to him, the findings will guide improvements in operational procedures, staff performance, logistics and the deployment of electoral technology ahead of the 2027 polls. He reaffirmed INEC’s commitment to credible elections, saying the commission remained determined to conduct polls that are free, fair, transparent, inclusive and peaceful. He described the mock accreditation and result upload exercise as an important milestone in the commission’s preparations, adding that the success of the process would depend on the cooperation and support of all stakeholders. He urged the media to use the opportunity to educate the public on the exercise, while encouraging residents to understand its purpose as a simulation aims at identifying and correcting operational weaknesses before the general elections.
